incidents.vector: Attackers chained Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager flaws, exploiting zero-day CVE-2026-20245 to create a rogue root account ('troot') on the edge orchestrator.
incidents.impact: Attackers gained the highest level of access and potential undetected visibility into the provider's entire internal network traffic; extensive anti-forensic activity prevented Mandiant from fully scoping the compromise.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack against the Indian automaker and its technology subsidiary; initial access vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Affected systems at Bajaj Auto and Bajaj Auto Technology Limited; company said containment and mitigation were so far successful and did not confirm data theft or a ransom demand.

incidents.vector: Data-theft and extortion intrusion by the World Leaks group (rebranded from Hunters International), detected weeks before public confirmation.
incidents.impact: Group published files allegedly stolen from the Apple/Tesla supplier, reportedly including Apple supplier specifications and Tesla manufacturing documents; Tata says operations were unaffected.

incidents.victim: StealC & Amadey malware infrastructure (140,000+ infected devices)
incidents.vector: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit, Europol and partners used RICO and court orders to seize 200+ command-and-control servers behind the Amadey loader and StealC infostealer.
incidents.impact: Disrupted infrastructure linked to 140,000+ infected computers; Microsoft severed control of 18,000+ victim devices. The tools (also used by Russia-affiliated actors against Ukraine) feed credentials into ransomware and fraud operations.

incidents.victim: FortiGate firewall operators worldwide (incl. NATO defense contractor)
incidents.attacker: Russia — Russian-speaking criminal group (initial access broker)
incidents.vector: Credential-stuffing and brute force against internet-exposed FortiGate interfaces, then a Go-based 'FortigateSniffer' tool abused FortiOS diagnostic commands to passively harvest credentials across 24 authentication protocols.
incidents.impact: 'FortiBleed' campaign exposed credentials for ~74,000–430,000 FortiGate devices across ~194 countries and harvested 110M+ credentials (RADIUS, NTLM, Kerberos); a NATO-aligned defense contractor reportedly had classified documents exfiltrated. CISA urged immediate Fortinet hardening.

incidents.victim: Salesforce customers via Klue app (Huntress, LastPass, HackerOne, Recorded Future, Jamf, Snyk, others)
incidents.vector: Attackers breached market-intelligence app vendor Klue and abused its OAuth tokens to pull customers' Salesforce CRM data.
incidents.impact: Extortion group Icarus stole and began leaking Salesforce data (business contacts, sales records) from at least a dozen tech and cyber firms; risk centers on targeted social-engineering follow-on. More victims expected.

incidents.victim: Transport for London (and US healthcare: SSM Health, Sutter Health)
incidents.vector: Members of the Scattered Spider group used social-engineering and credential theft to breach TfL's network in September 2024; two members pleaded guilty in the UK this week.
incidents.impact: The 2024 TfL attack forced all 28,000 employees to reset passwords in person, exposed Oyster refund data, and cost ~£29M ($38M). Defendants also linked to intrusions at US healthcare providers; sentencing set for mid-July.

incidents.victim: US bank customers (American Express, Bank of America, Chase, Wells Fargo, others)
incidents.vector: Algerian national 'SPOX' ran black-market sites (market0day.com, spoxy.us) selling phishing kits that cloned major US bank login pages, with hidden backdoors to keep harvesting victim data.
incidents.impact: ~595 phishing kits and ~5,600 identified victims; roughly $900K funneled through a crypto account over three years. The suspect was extradited from Spain and charged with bank-fraud conspiracy.

incidents.vector: Five malicious 'skills' on OpenClaw's ClawHub marketplace bypassed VirusTotal/ClawScan screening, delivering macOS infostealers and using file-padding evasion plus novel 'agentic' affiliate-injection and front-running schemes.
incidents.impact: Skills could steal credentials and files, manipulate agent behavior, and run autonomous financial-manipulation schemes; AMOS-linked C2 infrastructure remained active. OpenClaw removed the skills and banned the accounts.

incidents.victim: Consumers with Android TV streaming boxes (Popa/Vo1d botnet)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — residential proxy / ad fraud
incidents.vector: Malicious SDK ('Popa', tied to the Vo1d/Badbox lineage) bundled into off-brand Android TV boxes and pirated streaming apps enrolls devices into a residential-proxy network.
incidents.impact: Millions of consumer devices forced to relay traffic linked to ad fraud, account takeovers, and mass data-scraping (1.4M+ IPs in one scraping event); researchers tied the proxy pool to Israeli firm Alarum/NetNut, which disputes the findings.

incidents.victim: Southeast Asia cyber-scam / money-laundering ecosystem (Huione Group)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — fraud and money laundering
incidents.vector: Cambodia extradited Huione Group's former chairman Li Xiong to China; Huione provided banking, crypto-exchange and marketplace infrastructure that laundered proceeds from pig-butchering scams.
incidents.impact: FinCEN previously labeled Huione a primary money-laundering concern that washed at least $4B in illicit funds, including proceeds of North Korean cyber heists; the extradition is part of an intensifying regional crackdown on scam compounds.

incidents.vector: Microsoft DART found two unrelated actors in one intrusion: a ransomware actor exploited on-prem SharePoint and used legitimate tools (Velociraptor, Cloudflare tunnels, Zoho Assist) for persistence, while a second actor ran DLL sideloading and custom backdoors.
incidents.impact: Parallel threat activity established deep, lasting access while masking attribution and the full scope of the breach; the case highlights how multiple actors can operate simultaneously in one environment.

incidents.victim: North American academic, medical and military research institutions
incidents.vector: China-nexus actor exploited internet-facing REDCap research servers, deployed custom INFINITERED malware to harvest credentials, then abused Google Workspace content-compliance rules to silently BCC-forward sensitive email.
incidents.impact: Undetected for over a year (since Sept 2023), the actor pursued AI, cyber, medical, uncrewed-systems and national-defense research across multiple US/Canada institutions; Google disrupted the infrastructure and notified victims.

incidents.vector: Conti operators hacked into victim networks, encrypted data and stole files to extort payment; one Ukrainian member coded a malware 'loader' used in attacks.
incidents.impact: Ukrainian national Oleksii Lytvynenko pleaded guilty after extradition from Ireland; Conti attacked 1,000+ networks across 47 US states and 31 countries, netting at least $150M in ransoms. He faces up to 20 years.

incidents.victim: Higher-education and other Oracle PeopleSoft operators (100+ orgs)
incidents.vector: ShinyHunters (UNC6240) exploited a PeopleSoft zero-day (CVE-2026-35273, RCE, CVSS 9.8) in the Environment Management Hub, then used MeshCentral agents disguised as Azure services and an SSH 'fanout' script for lateral movement and defacement.
incidents.impact: Mandiant notified 100+ exposed organizations (68% higher education); several were compromised and had data published on the ShinyHunters leak site. Activity predated Oracle's June 10 advisory and ran as a zero-day.

incidents.victim: US security-clearance holders and government employees
incidents.vector: Suspected Chinese agents ran 13 fake consulting-company websites with AI-generated personas and photos, posting bogus 'consulting' jobs on hiring platforms to recruit clearance holders and pressure them for insider information.
incidents.impact: DOJ and FBI seized all 13 domains used to lure current and former clearance holders into revealing sensitive or classified information in exchange for cryptocurrency payments routed from overseas.
